observation_summary: The BracketingNthOrderBrentSolver was failing with a TooManyEvaluationsException because it was unable to rebalance the bracketing interval. The solver was consistently updating the same bracket point, leading to an infinite loop of evaluations until the limit was reached.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves replacing a simple, static targetY calculation with a more sophisticated weighted average formula that accounts for the 'aging' of the bracket points. This is a change to the underlying computational strategy (the algorithm) used to determine the next target point in the solver, rather than a simple value assignment or a missing guard condition.
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows a complete rewrite of the targetY calculation logic.
The bug report states that the aging feature was failing to rebalance the bracketing points, leading to an infinite loop.
The stack trace confirms the solver was hitting the evaluation limit during the solving process.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix is not just changing a constant or initializing a variable; it is implementing a new mathematical formula to calculate targetY based on dynamic aging factors.
There is no missing guard or condition; the logic for when to rebalance was already present, but the formula used for the rebalancing was computationally insufficient.
